1919138017.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tagged midline groove/raphe running vertically along the anterior abdominal wall from the xiphoid process to the pubic symphysis, formed by the interlacing aponeurotic fibers of the abdominal obliques and transversus abdominis.
1919138017.keyConcept: Linea alba: Fibrous midline abdominal raphe formed by decussation of bilateral abdominal wall aponeuroses extending from xiphoid to pubic symphysis.

968046907.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Protrusion situated inferior (below) and lateral to the pubic tubercle, emerging below the inguinal ligament into the upper thigh through the femoral ring and canal.
968046907.keyConcept: Femoral hernia: Emerges inferior and lateral to the pubic tubercle, below the inguinal ligament, presenting as a mass in the femoral triangle.

1315121096.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Protrusion situated superior (above) and medial to the pubic tubercle, emerging above the inguinal ligament along the course of the inguinal canal.
1315121096.keyConcept: Inguinal hernia: Emerges superior and medial to the pubic tubercle, above the inguinal ligament, passing through the inguinal canal.

782333975.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Longitudinal anteroposterior anatomical section displaying the abdominal and pelvic cavities from the anterior abdominal wall to the posterior vertebral column, outlining the greater sac, lesser sac (omental bursa), greater omentum, lesser omentum, and pelvic peritoneal pouches in sagittal profile.
782333975.keyConcept: Sagittal section of peritoneum: Displays vertical extent of peritoneal cavity including epiploic foramen, lesser omentum, and recto-vesical/recto-uterine pouches.

1536546560.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Triangular aperture in the aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle located superior and lateral to the pubic crest, bounded by the medial and lateral crura and intercrural fibers, transmitting the spermatic cord (or round ligament).
1536546560.keyConcept: Superficial inguinal ring: Triangular defect in external oblique aponeurosis through which the spermatic cord exits the inguinal canal.

1619910341.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval opening in the fascia transversalis located approximately 1.25 cm superior to the midinguinal point, immediately lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, representing the interior entrance to the inguinal canal.
1619910341.keyConcept: Deep inguinal ring: Oval opening in fascia transversalis situated lateral to inferior epigastric vessels transmitting structures into inguinal canal.

1201469963.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cylindrical cord emerging from the superficial inguinal ring and descending into the scrotum, containing the ductus deferens, testicular artery, pampiniform venous plexus, cremasteric artery, and autonomic nerves enclosed in three fascial coats.
1201469963.keyConcept: Spermatic cord: Traverses inguinal canal and exits superficial inguinal ring to suspend the testis; covered by external spermatic, cremasteric, and internal spermatic fascias.

33817005.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oblique ~4 cm intramuscular tunnel in the lower anterior abdominal wall running parallel and superior to the medial half of the inguinal ligament between the deep inguinal ring and the superficial inguinal ring.
33817005.keyConcept: Inguinal canal: ~4 cm oblique passage through lower abdominal wall transmitting the spermatic cord (or round ligament) and ilioinguinal nerve.

187436979.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large arterial trunk entering the femoral triangle behind the inguinal ligament at the midinguinal point, situated within the lateral compartment of the femoral sheath, lateral to the femoral vein.
187436979.keyConcept: Femoral artery: Enters anterior thigh deep to inguinal ligament at midinguinal point, lying lateral to femoral vein within the femoral sheath.

1350639618.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large deep vein ascending through the femoral triangle within the intermediate compartment of the femoral sheath, positioned medial to the femoral artery and lateral to the femoral canal.
1350639618.keyConcept: Femoral vein: Major venous vessel of lower limb ascending in femoral sheath medial to femoral artery before passing deep to inguinal ligament as external iliac vein.

768216970.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 6 indicates the pubic crest (between the pubic tubercle and pubic symphysis). The muscle originating from the pubic crest and anterior aspect of the pubic symphysis by two tendinous heads is the rectus abdominis muscle.
768216970.keyConcept: Rectus abdominis: Originates by two heads from pubic crest and pubic symphysis, inserting into costal cartilages 5–7 and xiphoid process.

1944464518.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 2 indicates the outer lip of the iliac crest. The external oblique abdominal muscle inserts by fleshy and aponeurotic fibers into the anterior half of the outer lip of the iliac crest.
1944464518.keyConcept: External oblique muscle: Lower fibers insert into the anterior half of the outer lip of the iliac crest.

1032516200.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 3 indicates the intermediate line of the iliac crest. The internal oblique abdominal muscle originates from the anterior two-thirds of the intermediate line of the iliac crest (as well as lateral two-thirds of inguinal ligament and thoracolumbar fascia).
1032516200.keyConcept: Internal oblique muscle: Originates from the intermediate line of the iliac crest (anterior two-thirds) between outer and inner lips.

407020956.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 5 indicates both bony attachment sites: the anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) laterally and the pubic tubercle medially. The dense fibrous band connecting these two landmarks is the inguinal ligament (Poupart's ligament), formed by the folded lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis.
407020956.keyConcept: Inguinal ligament (Poupart's): Spans from anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS) to pubic tubercle as the lower folded border of external oblique aponeurosis.

2025632533.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tag 4 indicates the sharp, prominent bony ridge on the upper aspect of the superior pubic ramus (pecten pubis), providing attachment for the pectineal (Cooper's) ligament, conjoint tendon, and lacunar ligament.
2025632533.keyConcept: Pectineal line (pecten pubis): Sharp ridge on superior pubic ramus giving attachment to the pectineal ligament and conjoint tendon.

1615651705.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Axial and sagittal reformatted contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) images displaying abdominal cross-sections with peritoneal reflections (parietal peritoneum in orange, visceral peritoneum in blue) outlining retroperitoneal and intraperitoneal viscera.
1615651705.keyConcept: Computed Tomography (CT) scan: Cross-sectional radiological imaging using X-ray attenuation to depict peritoneal spaces, retroperitoneum, and abdominal viscera.

1601812611.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The orange dotted outline lines the internal surface of the anterolateral abdominal wall, inferior surface of diaphragm, and pelvic parietes, representing the parietal layer of peritoneum (derived from somatopleuric mesoderm and innervated by somatic nerves).
1601812611.keyConcept: Parietal peritoneum: Lines abdominal and pelvic walls; sensitive to well-localized somatic pain (temperature, touch, pain) via spinal nerves.

739645329.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue continuous outline directly invests and covers the intraperitoneal abdominal viscera (liver, spleen, stomach, small intestine loops), representing the visceral layer of peritoneum (derived from splanchnopleuric mesoderm and innervated by autonomic afferents).
739645329.keyConcept: Visceral peritoneum: Invests abdominal organs; insensitive to somatic cutting/burning but sensitive to stretch, ischemia, and spasm (referred dull pain).
